rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all 10 compounds and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained components. A moderate temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Test whether the higher-temperature selectivity trend can fully separate the remaining close pair without slowing the method. Monitor the entire middle cluster because another gap narrowed at 50 C and may become limiting.

Use an intermediate temperature to balance the two temperature-sensitive gaps, with a shallower gradient to improve separation in the middle cluster. The current retention window suggests this extension should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test a slightly steeper gradient at the best temperature to bring the remaining R = 1.47 pair above threshold while shortening retention. The other middle-cluster gap has some margin at R = 2.18, so this is a promising balance between the competing separations.
The maximum CRF is already achieved; retain injection 5 as the benchmark and test a two-minute shorter gradient. This probes whether full resolution can be maintained with a shorter elution window.

Keep injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark and explore a substantially faster, hotter gradient. The nearly coeluting pair at 60 C may separate after an elution-order reversal as the gradient steepens, offering a different route to a shorter fully resolved method.

Return to the successful 55 C selectivity regime and combine a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower gradient. This tests whether both critical middle-cluster gaps can gain resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.
